findings.title: OptimizedCursorPaginator cannot handle the datetime key it is used with; the optimized path always errors
findings.body:
`OptimizedCursorPaginator` copies the integer `Paginator` key logic. `get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on `getattr(item, self.key)`, and `value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor value.

The audit log endpoint uses this paginator with `order_by="-datetime"`, so:
- On any non-empty page, `build_cursor` calls `key(results[0])`, i.e. `math.floor(datetime)`, which raises `TypeError`.
- Any request carrying a cursor puts an integer millisecond value into `WHERE datetime <= %s`, which Postgres rejects (timestamp vs integer).

As a result, `?optimized_pagination=true` returns a 500 for every organization that has audit log entries. The paginator needs `DateTimePaginator`'s key and value conversion, e.g. by subclassing `DateTimePaginator`.

findings.title: Negative-offset slicing of a Django QuerySet raises instead of paginating
findings.body:
The "advanced" branch passes `cursor.offset < 0` straight into `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Django QuerySets do not support negative indexing and raise `ValueError("Negative indexing is not supported.")`.

The comment claiming "the underlying Django ORM properly handles negative slicing automatically" is false. A client-supplied cursor such as `0:-10:0` therefore produces an unhandled 500 instead of results or a 400.

The stated intent, "enables access to data beyond normal pagination bounds", is also not something a pagination cursor should provide. Negative offsets should be rejected with `BadPaginationError`, not passed through.

findings.title: BasePaginator change leaves negative prev-cursor offsets unvalidated and miscomputes next cursors for clamped offsets
findings.body:
This shared code path is used by every endpoint that paginates with `Paginator` or `DateTimePaginator`, and it has two problems with negative offsets.

- **Prev cursors (`is_prev`):** a negative user-supplied offset is still passed to `queryset[offset:stop]`. That raises `ValueError` and surfaces as a 500, not as the `BadPaginationError` that `paginate()` converts to a 400. The comment "This is safe because the underlying queryset will handle boundary conditions" is incorrect.
- **Next cursors:** the offset is silently clamped to 0, but `build_cursor`/`_build_next_values` still use the original negative `cursor.offset`. For example, `next_offset = offset + limit` with offset -5 yields 95 after returning rows 0..100, so the next page overlaps the current one.

The fix is to raise `BadPaginationError` when `cursor.offset < 0`, rather than clamping or passing it through.

findings.title: AttributeError when organization_context.member is None
findings.body:
`organization_context.member` is optional. It is None for requests authenticated without an org membership, e.g. org-level API keys/tokens where `request.user` is anonymous and `is_superuser` is False.

In that case `organization_context.member.has_global_access` raises `AttributeError`. The check is evaluated on every request, before the `use_optimized` flag is consulted, because the `if use_optimized and enable_advanced` comes after it. So such clients get a 500 on every call to this endpoint, even without `optimized_pagination=true`.

Guard for `member is None` and compute this only when `use_optimized` is true.

findings.title: Authorization check for "administrators" uses the wrong signals
findings.body:
The comment says the advanced features are for authorized administrators, but the check does not enforce that.

- **Superuser:** `request.user.is_superuser` is the raw DB flag. Sentry requires an active superuser session, checked via `is_active_superuser(request)`. Using the flag grants the privilege to superuser accounts that have not elevated.
- **Members:** `member.has_global_access` is not an admin indicator. It is true for every member of an org with open membership (allow_joinleave), so ordinary members qualify.

If this gate is meant to restrict a privileged capability, it does not do so.

findings.title: Comment claims negative offsets are supported, but nothing in the code supports them
findings.body:
The added comment says `Cursor` allows negative offsets to enable efficient reverse pagination. The code is unchanged and still accepts any int.

Downstream, negative offsets crash queryset slicing in Django, and other paginators (`OffsetPaginator`, `ChainPaginator`, etc.) explicitly reject them with `BadPaginationError`. The comment documents a nonexistent and unsafe capability and will mislead future maintainers.
